rule: Nested types are dotted: `Outer.Inner#m`. ... a bare call to a member of the enclosing type → `Type#m`.
notes: call_type convention (SPEC names the six call_types but does not define direct vs method): a call with no written receiver is direct; a call with a written receiver (obj., this., super., a type name) is method; new/super(...)/this(...) are constructor. Inner, Leaf and Deep have no written constructor; the constructor calls are still high because the class is defined in the scan (SPEC: Java enum constants are high 'when the enum is in the scan' with no constructor written; the implicit default constructor is defined by the scanned class declaration). `note()` inside Inner is a bare call to a member of an enclosing type (Outer), so Outer#note. `Outer.Leaf` and `Leaf` name the same nested type.
